events.description: New York Times publishes 'Is Afghanistan's most wanted militant now its best hope for change?' profiling Sirajuddin Haqqani as a pragmatic statesman.
New York Times ran an op-ed in Sirajuddin Haqqani's name promising an inclusive political system; hosts say he could not have written it.
Taliban took over Afghanistan and reinstalled the Islamic Emirate 'a year and a half' after the op-ed.

Jalaluddin Haqqani, then commander of Taliban forces across southern Afghanistan, vowed a never-ending guerrilla war, rejected any new government of 'American, Russian and Indian stooges' and refused to give up bin Laden.
NYT claims Jalaluddin dispatched a convoy of relatives and allies to Kabul to back Karzai and a US airstrike hit the vehicles; hosts contrast this with his contemporaneous rejectionist statements.
Jalaluddin Haqqani helped Osama bin Laden escape Afghanistan.

From early 2002 to 2004 the Haqqanis organized the insurgency from North and South Waziristan, integrated Afghan Taliban with foreign fighters incl. al-Qaeda, and helped create the TTP alongside al-Qaeda.
US drone campaign 2004-2017: roughly 40% of strikes that killed top al-Qaeda leaders hit Haqqani-run safe houses in North Waziristan, usually also killing a mid/high-level Haqqani commander.
After Mullah Omar's death was revealed and the Taliban nearly fell apart, Siraj and his father put the Taliban back together.
Joscelyn testified before the Senate with written testimony dismantling Taliban-apologist arguments.
Bin Laden files released after advocacy by Joscelyn and Roggio; the Haqqanis, especially Siraj, feature in them.
Islamic State attacked Moscow, Russia and Iran this year; multiple plots inside the US homeland.
Within one week: floggings in Logar and Bamyan, 17 people flogged in Khost, one in Kabul and one in Faryab; new bans on women's voices and bus travel without masks.
Qatar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced a fourth Doha meeting in the near future.
Shortly after the NYT article, Barnett Rubin was photographed in China with the Taliban's ambassador to China.
Sirajuddin Haqqani 'popped up' in the UAE; The Diplomat quoted Rubin saying he no longer poses a threat to Americans (date not given by hosts).
NYT says the Haqqanis wanted peace in 2010; hosts say the bin Laden files and Haqqani actions at the time contradict this.

key_claims: The NYT profile is advocacy/PR for Sirajuddin Haqqani; the paper never acknowledged being played by the 2020 ghost-written op-ed.
Siraj's claim that no terrorist groups are in Afghanistan is demonstrably false: al-Qaeda and ISKP are present and the Haqqanis sheltered Zawahiri in Kabul.
The Haqqanis and al-Qaeda are at points indistinguishable: intermarriage, sheltering of bin Laden and his sons, 40% of AQ-leader drone strikes on Haqqani safe houses.
Jalaluddin Haqqani's own October 2001 statements (never-ending guerrilla war, 'stooges' government, 'all with us are Afghans') refute the NYT's detente narrative.
The Haqqanis organized the 2002-04 insurgency from Waziristan and helped create the TTP with al-Qaeda.
Hibatullah lacks military power; Siraj (and Yaqoob) are the real kingmakers, so Siraj's 'moderation' on girls' schooling is not credible.
ISKP is an enemy of the Haqqanis and Taliban and has attacked Russia and Iran and plotted in the US despite the Taliban's 'counterterrorism' promises.
The 2015-era near-collapse after Omar's death was reversed by Siraj and his father, showing the Haqqanis hold the Taliban together.
